countries.name: Kazakhstan
countries.description: Kazakh cuisine reflects the country's nomadic heritage, with an emphasis on meat, dairy products, and filling meals.

foods.name: Beshbarmak
foods.description: A traditional dish made with boiled meat served over broad noodles and topped with onion broth.
foods.culturalSignificance: Beshbarmak is often served at celebrations and family gatherings. It reflects Kazakhstan's nomadic traditions and the importance of hospitality.
foods.preparation: Meat is slowly simmered until tender, while broad noodles are cooked separately. The noodles are layered with sliced meat and onions softened in the cooking broth.

foods.name: Baursaki
foods.description: Small pieces of dough fried until golden brown, commonly served with tea or alongside other dishes.
foods.culturalSignificance: Baursaki are commonly prepared for holidays, weddings, and family gatherings. They symbolize hospitality and are often shared with guests.
foods.preparation: A soft yeast dough is allowed to rise, cut into small pieces, and deep-fried until puffed and golden. The warm pieces are often shared with tea.

foods.name: Kazy
foods.description: A traditional sausage made from seasoned horse meat, commonly boiled and served in slices.
foods.culturalSignificance: Kazy is considered a valued traditional food in Kazakhstan and is frequently served during celebrations and special occasions.
foods.preparation: Seasoned horse meat and fat are packed into a natural casing and traditionally cured or dried before being gently cooked. The finished sausage is sliced for serving.

foods.name: Kuurdak
foods.description: A hearty dish made by frying meat with onions, sometimes including potatoes and organ meats.
foods.culturalSignificance: Kuurdak reflects traditional livestock-based cooking and is often prepared as a filling meal shared among family members.
foods.preparation: Small pieces of meat are browned in fat with onions, then cooked until tender. Potatoes are often added to create a substantial one-pan meal.

countries.name: Kyrgyzstan
countries.description: Kyrgyz cuisine combines nomadic food traditions with influences from neighboring Central Asian cultures.

foods.name: Beshbarmak
foods.description: Boiled meat served with handmade noodles and broth, often prepared for important gatherings.
foods.culturalSignificance: Beshbarmak is a significant traditional meal in Kyrgyzstan and represents hospitality, respect for guests, and nomadic heritage.
foods.preparation: Meat is simmered with water and seasonings until tender. Handmade noodles are boiled and served with meat, onion sauce, and a little broth.

foods.name: Kuurdak
foods.description: A traditional fried meat dish prepared with onions and sometimes potatoes.
foods.culturalSignificance: Kuurdak has roots in nomadic cooking and remains a popular meal at home and during social gatherings.
foods.preparation: Meat and onions are fried together in a heavy pan, sometimes with potatoes. The dish is cooked until the meat is tender and the edges are lightly browned.

foods.name: Lagman
foods.description: A noodle dish featuring vegetables and meat in a flavorful sauce or broth.
foods.culturalSignificance: Lagman reflects cultural exchange along Central Asian trade routes and the influence of Uyghur and other regional cooking traditions.
foods.preparation: Wheat noodles are prepared separately, then topped with meat and vegetables cooked in a fragrant tomato-based sauce or broth.

foods.name: Ashlan-Fu
foods.description: A cold noodle dish with a tangy, spicy broth, often made with both wheat noodles and starch noodles.
foods.culturalSignificance: Ashlan-Fu is especially associated with Karakol and reflects Dungan culinary influences in Kyrgyzstan.
foods.preparation: Wheat and starch noodles are cooled, then combined with a tangy vinegar-chili broth and garnishes. The dish is typically served chilled.

countries.name: Turkmenistan
countries.description: Turkmen cuisine features meat, bread, rice, and soups shaped by pastoral traditions and regional influences.

foods.name: Plov
foods.description: A rice dish cooked with meat, carrots, onions, and seasonings.
foods.culturalSignificance: Plov is commonly prepared for family meals, celebrations, and gatherings. It represents hospitality and shared food traditions.
foods.preparation: Meat and onions are browned, carrots are softened, and rice is cooked with the seasoned ingredients in one pot until fluffy and fragrant.

foods.name: Dograma
foods.description: A traditional dish combining shredded meat, pieces of flatbread, onions, and broth.
foods.culturalSignificance: Dograma is closely associated with Turkmen hospitality and is often prepared for special gatherings and celebrations.
foods.preparation: Cooked lamb is shredded and mixed with small pieces of bread and sliced onions. Hot meat broth is poured over the mixture just before serving.

foods.name: Manty
foods.description: Steamed dumplings filled with seasoned meat and onions.
foods.culturalSignificance: Manty are part of a broader Central Asian dumpling tradition and are often prepared and enjoyed together by families.
foods.preparation: A simple dough is rolled thin, filled with seasoned meat and onion, and sealed into dumplings. The dumplings are then steamed until cooked through.

foods.name: Chorba
foods.description: A hearty soup typically made with meat, vegetables, and broth.
foods.culturalSignificance: Chorba is a traditional comfort food that reflects the importance of hearty soups in everyday Turkmen cooking.
foods.preparation: Meat is simmered in broth with vegetables such as potatoes, carrots, and onions. Slow cooking develops a rich and comforting soup.

countries.name: Uzbekistan
countries.description: Uzbek cuisine is known for rice dishes, breads, dumplings, and noodles influenced by Silk Road trade and agricultural traditions.

foods.name: Plov
foods.description: A famous Uzbek rice dish cooked with meat, carrots, onions, and spices.
foods.culturalSignificance: Plov is an important symbol of Uzbek hospitality and community. It is frequently served at weddings, holidays, and other celebrations.
foods.preparation: Meat, onions, and carrots are cooked in oil with seasonings. Rice is added and steamed above the mixture so the grains absorb the savory flavors.

foods.name: Samsa
foods.description: A baked pastry filled with seasoned meat, onions, or other ingredients.
foods.culturalSignificance: Samsa is a popular street food and traditional baked dish, often prepared in a clay tandoor oven.
foods.preparation: Seasoned fillings are enclosed in folded pastry and baked until golden, traditionally against the walls of a hot clay oven called a tandyr.

foods.name: Lagman
foods.description: A noodle dish served with meat and vegetables in a seasoned sauce or broth.
foods.culturalSignificance: Lagman reflects the cultural diversity of Uzbekistan and the historical exchange of cooking traditions along the Silk Road.
foods.preparation: Wheat noodles are served with a sautéed mix of meat, tomatoes, peppers, and onions. It may be prepared as a soup or with a thicker sauce.

foods.name: Manti
foods.description: Large steamed dumplings traditionally filled with meat and onions.
foods.culturalSignificance: Manti are commonly prepared for family meals and gatherings, reflecting the importance of shared cooking and dining traditions.
foods.preparation: Large meat-filled dumplings are wrapped in thin dough and steamed. They are commonly served warm with yogurt, sour cream, or a simple sauce.
